notes: WebSearch ran out partway (the session's search budget was spent), so most pages were reached directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: the campaign links on the Oklahoma Democratic Party's 'Our 2026 Candidates' page (https://www.okdemocrats.org/candidates) and the Tulsa County Republican Party's '2026 Oklahoma State Candidates' page, each opened and kept only when the site itself names the candidate and the office or district; county, city and state government pages; and a few campaign addresses checked by name lookup and then opened. Candidates with no keys below are ones for whom no such page stated anything a card may show.

No endorsed_by anywhere: no Oklahoma party page read calls anything an endorsement for these 2026 races (see ballot/lean/ok_endorsements.json, whose 'other_support' already holds the party listings). The Oklahoma Republican Party's site shows a CAPTCHA and was not requested.
Birth dates on the Wikipedia articles of Mike Mazzei and Cindy Byrd carry no citation in the infobox, so 'born' is left out for both.

Two sitting members' sites still carry 2024 wording (Danny Williams: 'Vote in Oklahoma 2024'; Suzanne Schreiber: footer 'Suzanne Schreiber for State House 2024'); they are kept as the member's own campaign sites, and the verifier may decide. Catherine Peters's site names her and 'VOTE NOVEMBER 3, 2026' and lists the Tulsa County Democratic Party among its endorsements, but does not print the district number; the state party's page links it under District 23.

Ballotpedia answered the kit's User-Agent with an empty page and was not used. Not found: campaign sites for Robert Franklin, Stacy Jo Adams, Max Wolfley, Albert Borrie and every county, judicial and city candidate in this part; Meloyde Blancett's site was found by name lookup (the party page links only social media).

Verifier (2026-10-03): every url re-opened (campaign sites, Grady County, the State Auditor's pages, Wikipedia, the Oklahoma Democratic Party's candidates page). Kept 28 findings; removed the websites of Jared Deck and Carri Hicks (429 on two tries); corrected the wording of three 'how' lines. Schreiber's site still has a 2024 footer but is the site the state party links for 2026 and names her for State Representative, so it is kept.
